{"parentUuid":"ab01f9e2-1df5-4a23-9be2-3d6044fa77b5","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"d1541fe7-ff93-4704-9ad4-ca5d37faa022","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FhqDLrL1D2xVYwcVLMg92s","type":"tool_result","content":"title:\tSpec: KCFC web CMS\nstate:\tOPEN\nauthor:\tiaishikb-rgb\nlabels:\tready-for-agent, spec\ncomments:\t0\nassignees:\t\nprojects:\t\nmilestone:\t\nissue-type:\t\nparent:\t\nsub-issues:\t\nsub-issues-completed:\t\nblocked-by:\t\nblocking:\t\nnumber:\t1\n--\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon College Finance Club (KCFC) is run by three Presidents and about eight Officers, and nearly everything is communicated by email to financeclub@kenyon.edu. The current Wix site shows no officers, no meeting time and no events, its Contact Us link goes back to the homepage, and its Resources headings have nothing under them, so a first-year or an alumnus can reasonably conclude the club is dead. Only one or two people can update it, there is no way to give Officers limited access, and nothing stops an unfinished stock pitch from going out under the club's name in front of William Blair alumni. When leadership changes there is no clean way to hand over or take away access.\n\nVocabulary below is defined in `CONTEXT.md`.\n\n## Users\n\n- **Presidents** (3, Admin role): run the club, review everything, sign off on what goes public.\n- **Officers** (about 8, Editor role): contribute meeting announcements, pitch writeups and alumni call recaps. Not technical; an announcement must take under two minutes.\n- **Visitors** (never log in): prospective members (first-years and sophomores) asking \"what is this, do I need experience, when and where do you meet\"; current members looking for event details, the resume review form and the Analyst Program; alumni and recruiters (including William Blair) checking leadership and activity before an event or pitch review.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with a local admin console on the Club laptop and a static public site. Presidents and Officers sign in with individual accounts. Officers write Posts and save Drafts; only Presidents publish, manage Pages, and manage Users. A Publish run turns everything Published into a static site on GitHub Pages. The first thing a Visitor sees is the next meeting. Nothing unreviewed reaches the public site, and an Officer who leaves loses access without anyone changing a shared password.\n\n## The 7 required capabilities, in KCFC's words\n\n1. **Login.** Presidents and Officers sign in and out with their Kenyon email and their own password. Passwords are stored hashed, never as text. A President sets the first password face to face, and resets lost passwords in person. Signed in on the shared Club laptop, a User is signed out after about 2 hours idle.\n2. **Two roles.** *Admin* (the three Presidents) can do everything. *Editor* (Officers) can write and edit only their own Posts, save them as Drafts and delete their own Drafts. An Editor cannot publish, cannot delete a Published Post, cannot touch any Page, and cannot see user management. These limits are enforced by the system itself, including when an Editor types a restricted address straight into the browser (the WordPress \"Editor can trash the About page\" problem from the field notes).\n3. **Posts.** One kind of Post (meeting announcement, pitch writeup, or alumni call recap), no categories. Each has a title, slug, Markdown body, Draft/Published status, author and timestamps, and can be created, read, updated and deleted under the role rules above. The slug is made from the title once and never changes when the title is edited; only an Admin can edit it. An Editor's edit to a Published Post turns it back into a Draft until a President republishes it. An Admin's edit leaves it Published.\n4. **Pages.** Lasting club information: Homepage, About, Leadership, Analyst Program, Join (for prospective members), Recruiting (for current members: resume review form link, standing guides). Same fields as a Post, but only Admins may create, edit, or delete them. Published Pages appear in the public Navigation in an order an Admin sets. The Homepage opens with the **next-meeting line** (plain text such as \"Next meeting: Wed Oct 28, 7 pm, Oden 110\", updated by a President the night before), then the contact email, then the latest Posts.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts of Drafts, Published items and Pending changes (Admins also see active and Deactivated User counts), a one-click \"New Post\" button, and a \"pending changes\" banner so nobody assumes saved work is already Live. A content list, newest first, filterable by status (All / Published / Draft, with counts) and type; Editors see only their own Posts. An editor with a side-by-side Preview of the sanitized Markdown, labelled \"Draft, not Live\" when it is not.\n6. **User management (Admin only).** Presidents create Users, change Roles, and Deactivate Users. A Deactivated User cannot sign in, and an open session ends at their next action. Users are never deleted: when seniors graduate in May their old Posts keep their name but they cannot log in. A Deactivated User can be reactivated. At least one President must always stay active, and a President cannot deactivate themselves.\n7. **Public site and publish.** Visitors see only Published content. Markdown is sanitized (see below). Navigation is built from Published Pages plus a link to the Posts listing (newest first, title and date). Each Post shows a byline, \"By <name>, <date>\", never an email address; Pages show none. `cms publish` (Admin only, usually run right before a meeting) writes `site/` with relative paths only and deploys it to GitHub Pages. Marking an item Published has a \"Publish this?\" confirm. There is no change summary; a mistake is fixed by unpublishing and running it again.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As a first-year, I want the next meeting's date, time and place at the very top of the homepage, so that I know when and where to show up.\n2. As a prospective member, I want a Join page saying what the club does and whether I need experience, so that I can decide whether to come.\n3. As a prospective member, I want the contact email on the homepage, so that I can ask a question.\n4. As a current member, I want a Recruiting page with the resume review form link, so that I can request a review without digging through email.\n5. As a current member, I want a list of Posts, newest first, so that I can find the latest announcement.\n6. As a current member, I want to read about the Analyst Program on its own page, so that I know what it involves.\n7. As an alumnus, I want a Leadership page, so that I know who runs the club before I speak at an event.\n8. As a recruiter or William Blair alumnus, I want to read reviewed pitch writeups and recaps, so that I can see the club's work, and I want to see only reviewed work.\n9. As a Visitor, I want links that keep working, so that a shared link to a Post is never dead.\n10. As a Visitor, I want to see an author's name but never their email address, so that student contact details stay private.\n11. As a Visitor, I want the site to work when served from a GitHub Pages subfolder, so that no page or link is broken.\n12. As an Officer, I want my own account, so that I never share a password.\n13. As an Officer, I want to sign in with my Kenyon email, so that it is easy to remember.\n14. As an Officer, I want to write a meeting announcement in under two minutes, so that updating the site is not a chore.\n15. As an Officer, I want to write in plain Markdown with a preview beside it, so that I can see what the Post will look like.\n16. As an Officer, I want to save my work as a Draft, so that I can finish it later.\n17. As an Officer, I want my Draft to stay private until a President publishes it, so that nothing goes public by accident.\n18. As an Officer, I want to see and edit only my own Posts, so that I do not break another team's pitch before the William Blair presentation.\n19. As an Officer, I want to delete my own abandoned Drafts, so that my list stays clean.\n20. As an Officer, I want to be told clearly when I cannot do something, so that I do not think the site is broken.\n21. As an Officer, I want a \"Draft, not Live\" label on my preview, so that I do not think members can already see it.\n22. As an Officer, I want to be signed out automatically on the shared laptop, so that the next person cannot use my account.\n23. As an Officer, I want my name on my Post after I graduate, so that my work keeps its credit.\n24. As a President, I want to review every Draft in one list, so that I can sign off before publishing.\n25. As a President, I want to see all Drafts filtered by status with counts, so that I know what still needs attention.\n26. As a President, I want to edit any Post, so that I can fix a pitch writeup before it goes out.\n27. As a President, I want an Officer's edit to a Published Post to turn it back to Draft, so that no unreviewed change goes out.\n28. As a President, I want a \"Publish this?\" confirm, so that I do not publish by mis-click.\n29. As a President, I want to unpublish a Post or Page, so that I can take down a mistake and rerun the publish.\n30. As a President, I want to delete a Post or Page after an \"are you sure?\" step, so that deletion is deliberate.\n31. As a President, I want only Presidents to edit or delete Leadership and Analyst Program (and every other Page), so that Officers cannot damage official pages.\n32. As a President, I want to set the order of Pages in Navigation, so that the menu reads sensibly.\n33. As a President, I want to edit the Homepage's next-meeting line, so that the first thing a first-year sees is current.\n34. As a President, I want a banner showing pending changes, so that I know the live site is behind.\n35. As a President, I want to run `cms publish` right before a meeting, so that the public site is up to date.\n36. As a President, I want to create accounts and set the first password in person, so that no email system is required.\n37. As a President, I want to reset a lost password in person, so that Officers are never locked out.\n38. As a President, I want to change a User's role, so that a new President can be made Admin at turnover.\n39. As a President, I want to deactivate an outgoing Officer, so that they can no longer sign in.\n40. As a President, I want a deactivated User to lose access immediately, even if signed in, so that handover is clean.\n41. As a President, I want to reactivate a User, so that a returning Officer does not need a new account.\n42. As a President, I want the system to refuse to deactivate the last active President or myself, so that the club cannot lock itself out.\n43. As a President, I want an Editor who types an Admin address into the browser to be refused, so that restrictions are real and not just hidden menu items.\n44. As a President, I want dashboard counts, so that I can see the state of the site at a glance.\n45. As a President, I want Posts to keep their author when the user is Deactivated, so that the archive stays accurate.\n46. As a President, I want Markdown to be sanitized everywhere it renders, so that nobody can inject a script into the club's site.\n47. As a President, I want the database file never to be committed, so that accounts and Drafts stay private.\n48. As a President, I want to hand the whole system to next year's Presidents without a shared password, so that continuity does not depend on one person.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture** follows ADR-001 (admin console local, public site static, explicit publish) and ADR-002 (FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, argon2, no frontend framework). The dependency set in `pyproject.toml` is fixed; adding any dependency needs asking first.\n- **Roles:** exactly two, Admin and Editor. Permission checks live in one place on the server and every admin route goes through it, so direct URL access is refused as reliably as hidden menus. Editor-restricted requests return a refusal or redirect, never the page.\n- **Content model:** Post and Page share fields (title, slug, Markdown body, status Draft/Published, author, created and updated timestamps). A Post has no kind or category. Pages additionally have a navigation order. Status for a Page is Draft or Published like a Post.\n- **Slug rules:** generated from the title on first save, unique, immutable on title edit, editable only by an Admin, no redirects from old slugs. Navigation and the Posts listing use slugs, so links stay stable.\n- **Editing rules:** an Editor can read and change only Posts they authored; an Editor's save on a Published Post sets it to Draft. An Admin's save keeps its status. Marking Published is Admin-only and goes through a \"Publish this?\" confirm.\n- **Delete rules:** Admin can delete any Post or Page after a confirm step; an Editor can delete only their own Drafts. Unpublish (return to Draft) is separate from delete.\n- **Users:** email and argon2-hashed password; roles; active flag. Deactivating sets the flag; every request checks it, so an open session is refused at the next action. Users are never deleted. Guard rails: cannot deactivate or demote yourself, the last active Admin cannot be deactivated or demoted. First password is set by an Admin; no forced change at first sign-in; no email-based reset. Sessions are signed cookies with an idle timeout of about 2 hours.\n- **CSRF:** every state-changing form carries a CSRF token.\n- **Sanitizing:** every rendered body goes through the sanitizer, both in the admin Preview and in the exported site. Scripts, event handlers such as `onerror`, iframes and `javascript:` links are stripped. Plain formatting, headings, lists and normal links stay. Raw HTML embeds are not supported and images are out of scope.\n- **Publish:** the exporter renders only Published Posts and Pages into `site/` using relative paths only (never `href=\"/...\"` or `src=\"/...\"`): Homepage (with the next-meeting line and latest Posts), each Page, the Posts listing, each Post with its byline, and Navigation built from Published Pages in Admin-set order plus the Posts listing. Drafts never leave the database. `site/` is generated, never hand-edited. Deployment pushes `site/` to the `gh-pages` branch. \"Pending changes\" is the difference between current Published content and what the last Publish run wrote.\n- **Console screens:** login/logout, dashboard (counts, New Post, pending changes banner), content list with status and type filters and counts, editor with side-by-side Preview, Page ordering, user management (Admin only).\n- **Seed and demo:** the existing seed script builds a demo database with one Admin and one Editor.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- A good test checks external behaviour only: what a signed-in role sees, can do, and is refused, and what ends up in the generated site. It does not assert on internal functions or database layout.\n- **Seam 1, the HTTP app,** through the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. This covers login and logout, role permissions (including direct URL access), Post/Page CRUD, slug immutability, Editor-edit-reverts-to-Draft, own-Drafts-only, deactivation, last-Admin and self-deactivation guards, CSRF rejection, idle timeout, dashboard counts, filters and preview.\n- **Seam 2, the site export,** through the existing render function (`render_site(out_dir)`). It covers only-Published content, Drafts absent, sanitizer behaviour (scripts, `onerror`, iframes, `javascript:` links stripped; headings, lists, links kept), navigation order, byline text with no email, and no root-absolute `href`/`src`.\n- No new seams are needed; these two already exist and are the highest available. The existing front-door tests must keep passing.\n- **Prior art:** `tests/test_t00.py` (client and `render_site` tests), `tests/conftest.py` (`client_as` fixture, written so access-control tests are one line).\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nExplicitly NOT building:\n\n[project]\nname = \"iphs400-mp2-cms\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\ndescription = \"IPHS 400 MP2 — a small web CMS with a local admin console and a static public site\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.12\"\ndependencies = [\n    \"fastapi>=0.115\",\n    \"uvicorn[standard]>=0.32\",\n    \"jinja2>=3.1\",\n    \"python-multipart>=0.0.12\",   # form posts\n    \"itsdangerous>=2.2\",          # signed session cookies\n    \"argon2-cffi>=23.1\",          # password hashing (never store plain passwords)\n    \"markdown-it-py>=3.0\",        # Markdown -> HTML\n    \"nh3>=0.2\",                   # HTML sanitizer (strips <script> etc.)\n    \"ghp-import>=2.1\",            # push site/ to the gh-pages branch\n]\n\n[dependency-groups]\ndev = As a current member, I want to read about the Analyst Program on its own page, so that I know what it involves.\n7. As an alumnus, I want a Leadership page, so that I know who runs the club before I speak at an event.\n8. As a recruiter or William Blair alumnus, I want to read reviewed pitch writeups and recaps, so that I can see the club's work, and I want to see only reviewed work.\n9. As a Visitor, I want links that keep working, so that a shared link to a Post is never dead.\n10. As a Visitor, I want to see an author's name but never their email address, so that student contact details stay private.\n11. As a Visitor, I want the site to work when served from a GitHub Pages subfolder, so that no page or link is broken.\n12. As an Officer, I want my own account, so that I never share a password.\n13. As an Officer, I want to sign in with my Kenyon email, so that it is easy to remember.\n14. As an Officer, I want to write a meeting announcement in under two minutes, so that updating the site is not a chore.\n15. As an Officer, I want to write in plain Markdown with a preview beside it, so that I can see what the Post will look like.\n16. As an Officer, I want to save my work as a Draft, so that I can finish it later.\n17. As an Officer, I want my Draft to stay private until a President publishes it, so that nothing goes public by accident.\n18. As an Officer, I want to see and edit only my own Posts, so that I do not break another team's pitch before the William Blair presentation.\n19. As an Officer, I want to delete my own abandoned Drafts, so that my list stays clean.\n20. As an Officer, I want to be told clearly when I cannot do something, so that I do not think the site is broken.\n21. As an Officer, I want a \"Draft, not Live\" label on my preview, so that I do not think members can already see it.\n22. As an Officer, I want to be signed out automatically on the shared laptop, so that the next person cannot use my account.\n23. As an Officer, I want my name on my Post after I graduate, so that my work keeps its credit.\n24. As a President, I want to review every Draft in one list, so that I can sign off before publishing.\n25. As a President, I want to see all Drafts filtered by status with counts, so that I know what still needs attention.\n26. As a President, I want to edit any Post, so that I can fix a pitch writeup before it goes out.\n27. As a President, I want an Officer's edit to a Published Post to turn it back to Draft, so that no unreviewed change goes out.\n28. As a President, I want a \"Publish this?\" confirm, so that I do not publish by mis-click.\n29. As a President, I want to unpublish a Post or Page, so that I can take down a mistake and rerun the publish.\n30. As a President, I want to delete a Post or Page after an \"are you sure?\" step, so that deletion is deliberate.\n31. As a President, I want only Presidents to edit or delete Leadership and Analyst Program (and every other Page), so that Officers cannot damage official pages.\n32. As a President, I want to set the order of Pages in Navigation, so that the menu reads sensibly.\n33. As a President, I want to edit the Homepage's next-meeting line, so that the first thing a first-year sees is current.\n34. As a President, I want a banner showing pending changes, so that I know the live site is behind.\n35. As a President, I want to run `cms publish` right before a meeting, so that the public site is up to date.\n36. As a President, I want to create accounts and set the first password in person, so that no email system is required.\n37. As a President, I want to reset a lost password in person, so that Officers are never locked out.\n38. As a President, I want to change a User's role, so that a new President can be made Admin at turnover.\n39. As a President, I want to deactivate an outgoing Officer, so that they can no longer sign in.\n40. As a President, I want a deactivated User to lose access immediately, even if signed in, so that handover is clean.\n41. As a President, I want to reactivate a User, so that a returning Officer does not need a new account.\n42. As a President, I want the system to refuse to deactivate the last active President or myself, so that the club cannot lock itself out.\n43. As a President, I want an Editor who types an Admin address into the browser to be refused, so that restrictions are real and not just hidden menu items.\n44. As a President, I want dashboard counts, so that I can see the state of the site at a glance.\n45. As a President, I want Posts to keep their author when the user is Deactivated, so that the archive stays accurate.\n46. As a President, I want Markdown to be sanitized everywhere it renders, so that nobody can inject a script into the club's site.\n47. As a President, I want the database file never to be committed, so that accounts and Drafts stay private.\n48. As a President, I want to hand the whole system to next year's Presidents without a shared password, so that continuity does not depend on one person.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture** follows ADR-001 (admin console local, public site static, explicit publish) and ADR-002 (FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, argon2, no frontend framework). The dependency set in `pyproject.toml` is fixed; adding any dependency needs asking first.\n- **Roles:** exactly two, Admin and Editor. Permission checks live in one place on the server and every admin route goes through it, so direct URL access is refused as reliably as hidden menus. Editor-restricted requests return a refusal or redirect, never the page.\n- **Content model:** Post and Page share fields (title, slug, Markdown body, status Draft/Published, author, created and updated timestamps). A Post has no kind or category. Pages additionally have a navigation order. Status for a Page is Draft or Published like a Post.\n- **Slug rules:** generated from the title on first save, unique, immutable on title edit, editable only by an Admin, no redirects from old slugs. Navigation and the Posts listing use slugs, so links stay stable.\n- **Editing rules:** an Editor can read and change only Posts they authored; an Editor's save on a Published Post sets it to Draft. An Admin's save keeps its status. Marking Published is Admin-only and goes through a \"Publish this?\" confirm.\n- **Delete rules:** Admin can delete any Post or Page after a confirm step; an Editor can delete only their own Drafts. Unpublish (return to Draft) is separate from delete.\n- **Users:** email and argon2-hashed password; roles; active flag. Deactivating sets the flag; every request checks it, so an open session is refused at the next action. Users are never deleted. Guard rails: cannot deactivate or demote yourself, the last active Admin cannot be deactivated or demoted. First password is set by an Admin; no forced change at first sign-in; no email-based reset. Sessions are signed cookies with an idle timeout of about 2 hours.\n- **CSRF:** every state-changing form carries a CSRF token.\n- **Sanitizing:** every rendered body goes through the sanitizer, both in the admin Preview and in the exported site. Scripts, event handlers such as `onerror`, iframes and `javascript:` links are stripped. Plain formatting, headings, lists and normal links stay. Raw HTML embeds are not supported and images are out of scope.\n- **Publish:** the exporter renders only Published Posts and Pages into `site/` using relative paths only (never `href=\"/...\"` or `src=\"/...\"`): Homepage (with the next-meeting line and latest Posts), each Page, the Posts listing, each Post with its byline, and Navigation built from Published Pages in Admin-set order plus the Posts listing. Drafts never leave the database. `site/` is generated, never hand-edited. Deployment pushes `site/` to the `gh-pages` branch. \"Pending changes\" is the difference between current Published content and what the last Publish run wrote.\n- **Console screens:** login/logout, dashboard (counts, New Post, pending changes banner), content list with status and type filters and counts, editor with side-by-side Preview, Page ordering, user management (Admin only).\n- **Seed and demo:** the existing seed script builds a demo database with one Admin and one Editor.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- A good test checks external behaviour only: what a signed-in role sees, can do, and is refused, and what ends up in the generated site. It does not assert on internal functions or database layout.\n- **Seam 1, the HTTP app,** through the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures. This covers login and logout, role permissions (including direct URL access), Post/Page CRUD, slug immutability, Editor-edit-reverts-to-Draft, own-Drafts-only, deactivation, last-Admin and self-deactivation guards, CSRF rejection, idle timeout, dashboard counts, filters and preview.\n- **Seam 2, the site export,** through the existing render function (`render_site(out_dir)`). It covers only-Published content, Drafts absent, sanitizer behaviour (scripts, `onerror`, iframes, `javascript:` links stripped; headings, lists, links kept), navigation order, byline text with no email, and no root-absolute `href`/`src`.\n- No new seams are needed; these two already exist and are the highest available. The existing front-door tests must keep passing.\n- **Prior art:** `tests/test_t00.py` (client and `render_site` tests), `tests/conftest.py` (`client_as` fixture, written so access-control tests are one line).\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nExplicitly NOT building:\n\n[project]\nname = \"iphs400-mp2-cms\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\ndescription = \"IPHS 400 MP2 — a small web CMS with a local admin console and a {"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"4041ad69-0861-41ba-bd16-245831342e3a","hash":"6a18e2582cc0cb4e763ac88861f0a3742208115ccd82a8e3eb8976850a6ce7a1","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SyeLWJtQqNKpMXZQe3M7j3","type":"tool_result","content":"=== app/main.py\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import settings\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/admin\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\"}\n        )\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    # Your ticket work plugs in here, e.g.\n    #   from app.routes import posts\n    #   app.include_router(posts.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n=== app/settings.py\n\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n\nSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\nDATABASE_PATH = Path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", ROOT / \"cms.db\"))\nSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"My CMS\")\n# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")\n=== app/cli.py\n\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n            return 1\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\n             str(settings.SITE)],\n        )\n        if result.returncode == 0:\n            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n        return result.returncode\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n=== app/publish.py\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n            home_path=\"index.html\",\n        )\n    )\n    return out\n=== scripts/seed_demo.py\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Create demo data so a grader (and you) can use the CMS immediately.\n\n    uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nT00 has nothing to seed. As you build content types, extend this so it creates:\n  - one admin and one editor (passwords read from .env, never hard-coded)\n  - a few posts and pages, at least one draft and one published\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    admin_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n    editor_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")\n    if not admin_pw or not editor_pw:\n        print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env \"\n              \"(copy .env.example).\")\n        return 1\n\n    # TODO (your tickets): create the users, then the demo content.\n    print(\"Nothing to seed yet: no content types exist. \"\n          \"Extend scripts/seed_demo.py as you build T01+.\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n=== tests/conftest.py\n\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a client that is logged\nin as a seeded user of that role — it works as soon as your login route exists,\nso access-control tests stay one line:\n\n    def test_editor_cannot_manage_users(client_as):\n        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client() -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as():\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app())\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"]},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        if response.status_code == 404:\n            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n=== tests/test_t00.py\n\"\"\"T00: the walking skeleton. These pass in the fresh template.\n\nDo not delete them. If a change breaks them, the change broke the app's front\ndoor.\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef test_admin_console_answers(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/admin\")\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n    assert \"hello admin\" in response.text.lower()\n\n\ndef test_public_home_answers(client):\n    response = client.get(\"/\")\n    assert response.status_code == 200\n\n\ndef test_publish_writes_a_site(tmp_path):\n    from app.publish import render_site\n\n    out = render_site(tmp_path / \"site\")\n    assert (out / \"index.html\").exists() and (out / \"style.css\").exists()\n\n\ndef test_published_html_uses_relative_paths(tmp_path):\n    \"\"\"Root-absolute paths break on GitHub Pages project URLs (rubric F2).\"\"\"\n    from app.publish import render_site\n\n    html = (render_site(tmp_path / \"site\") / \"index.html\").read_text()\n    assert 'href=\"/' not in html and 'src=\"/' not in html\n=== templates/base.html\n<!doctype html>\n<html lang=\"en\">\n<head>\n  <meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n  <meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n  <title>{% block title %}{{ title }}{% endblock %}</title>\n  <link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"{{ css_path | default('style.css') }}\">\n</head>\n<body>\n  <header><a href=\"{{ home_path | default('index.html') }}\">{{ title }}</a></header>\n  <main>{% block content %}{% endblock %}</main>\n  <footer><small>IPHS 400 Mini-Project #2</small></footer>\n</body>\n</html>\n=== templates/admin/hello.html\n{% extends \"base.html\" %}\n{% block content %}\n  <h1>T00: hello admin</h1>\n  <p>The stack works. Now build ticket T01.</p>\n{% endblock %}\n=== docs/adr/ADR-002-stack.md\n# ADR-002: FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, with no frontend framework\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nThe project has to be readable by someone who has never built a web application,\ngradable from a clean clone, and finishable in two weeks on a $20 plan. Options\nconsidered: Django (batteries included, but a large amount of generated code to\nread), Flask (similar to FastAPI here), a JavaScript stack (a second language and\na build step), and FastAPI with server-rendered templates.\n\n## Decision\n\nFastAPI with Jinja2 templates, SQLite for storage, argon2 for password hashing,\nand an HTML sanitizer for user Markdown. No frontend framework, no build step.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Every page is server-rendered, so \"view source\" shows what the code produced,\n  which makes debugging visible.\n- SQLite is a single file, so a grader can seed and inspect it easily. It is\n  gitignored; `scripts/seed_demo.py` rebuilds it.\n- No build step means the file you preview is the file that ships.\n- Interactive flourishes (live preview without reload, drag-and-drop) cost more\n  here than in a JavaScript stack. That is an accepted trade.","is_error":false}]}}

admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. {"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"4041ad69-0861-41ba-bd16-245831342e3a","hash":"8e891a90c602c7dca3e3891250ee5873cccefa2f17d3e83492d9954a597ef47b","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_012Xi6ASozGCFf3KYsi7ZLJK","content":"Launching skill: tdd"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/skills/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `GLOSSARY.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\" Give each proposed seam a one-line note on what it catches and what it misses.\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n"}]}}

{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"4041ad69-0861-41ba-bd16-245831342e3a","hash":"0a203cf7b6816c86cfc3237bab42383b74efb6fcb619016cf0f954a9b02d3633","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_01Ruh4hz2VRRkZVFbpwmbVVs","content":"Launching skill: code-review"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nSearch the repo for every file that documents how code should be written. When `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, it must be on the list.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\nIssue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: since HEAD (uncommitted T01 work), spec #1, ticket #2"}]}}

{"parentUuid":"fd1bcc23-4158-47ae-b099-d100cd4fe69f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"d1541fe7-ff93-4704-9ad4-ca5d37faa022","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nSearch the repo for every file that documents how code should be written. When `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, it must be on the list.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\nIssue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: since HEAD (uncommitted T01 work), spec #1, ticket #2"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"38b2bb7b-ea54-49de-a425-ea643cc26d8c","timestamp":"2026-10-15T03:06:06.211Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01Ruh4hz2VRRkZVFbpwmbVVs","session_id":"4041ad69-0861-41ba-bd16-245831342e3a","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"4041ad69-0861-41ba-bd16-245831342e3a","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

Any non-form POST, such as JSON, gets 403.\n- The `client_as` fixture still contains a `pytest.skip` for a 404 on `/login`. That is dead code now.\n\n**T00 test change.** I judge it reasonable. The ticket's requirements conflict, because anonymous `/admin` must redirect while \"T00 tests still pass\". The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Standards review of uncommitted T01 work (read-only)**\n\n**Hard violations**\n1. **Secret key fallback.** `app/settings.py` falls back to `\"dev-only-not-for-production\"` when `CMS_SECRET_KEY` is unset. This line was not changed in the diff, but T01 is the first code to sign cookies with it. CLAUDE.md says to read secrets from the environment. With the fallback, anyone can forge a session cookie, including `user_id` and `csrf`, on a clone that has no `.env`. Fix: fail at startup if the variable is missing. Tests would set it in `conftest`.\n2. **Vocabulary.** CLAUDE.md says to use CONTEXT.md vocabulary and not to use two words for one thing. CONTEXT.md calls it **Sign-in** and **Sign-out**.\n   - The code uses both words: `NotSignedIn` and \"Sign in\" in the templates, but `/login`, `/logout`, `login.html`, `to_login`, `login_form`, `GENERIC_ERROR` and `test_t01_login.py`.\n   - Either rename the code to match the glossary or add \"login\" to the glossary.\n   - I'd rate this a soft violation, because the routes `/login` and `/logout` are probably fixed by the ticket.\n3. **Glossary filename conflict.** `docs/agents/domain.md` still says `GLOSSARY.md`, which contradicts the CLAUDE.md course rule. Not in the diff, but flag it.\n\n**Security checks (all pass unless noted)**\n- **CSRF:** `csrf_protect` is an app-wide dependency, so it covers every non-safe method, including the `/admin/{rest}` catch-all. It uses `compare_digest`. Both forms carry the token. Tests cover a missing token and a forged one.\n- **Session cookie:** HttpOnly is Starlette's default. `SameSite=lax` is set. `max_age=None` makes it a browser-session cookie. `https_only` is off, which is acceptable for a local-only console.\n- **Session fixation:** `request.session.clear()` runs at sign-in, so there is no fixation.\n- **Logout and replay:** the session is a client-side signed cookie. Logout only clears the cookie, so a replayed old cookie still works until it expires or the user is deactivated. This is a judgement call. The 2-hour idle limit and the per-request `active` check limit the exposure.\n- **Passwords:** argon2 hashes, a dummy hash on unknown emails, and one generic error message. Nothing logs passwords. `seed_demo` prints emails only.\n- **Dependencies:** `itsdangerous` and `argon2-cffi` are already in `pyproject.toml`, so nothing new was added.\n- **Relative paths:** `action=\"/login\"`, `action=\"/logout\"` and the redirects are absolute paths. They are in admin-only templates, which the hard constraint doesn't cover. Make sure `base.html` and these templates never get rendered into `site/`.\n\n**Smells (judgement calls)**\n- **Primitive Obsession and Shotgun Surgery:** the role strings `\"admin\"` and `\"editor\"` are repeated in the `db.py` CHECK, `User.role: str`, `require_role(\"admin\")`, `seed_users` and the conftest dict. A `Role` enum or constants would fix this.\n- **Duplicated Code:**\n  - `routes/auth.py` repeats `from app.main import templates` twice, inside the functions. This is a circular-import workaround, and the smell is the dependency from a route module back to `main`. Move `templates` into its own module such as `app/templating.py`.\n  - The `tests/conftest.py` `_csrf` helper duplicates `csrf_of` in `test_t01_login.py`.\n  - The `SELECT ... WHERE email` lookup in `users.py` is a minor repeat.\n- **Duplicated Code or Speculative Generality:** `Depends(auth.require_user)` is attached both on the `admin` router and on `admin_home`'s `user` parameter. The router-level one is redundant, though harmless, since FastAPI caches the dependency.\n- **Speculative Generality:** `require_role(*roles)` has no real caller; its only use is a probe in a test. It supports the later admin-only tickets, and the spec may require it. Check the spec. The `create_app(clock=...)` injection is justified by the idle-timeout tests.\n- **Mysterious Name:** `to_login` and `admin_unknown` are mild. `get_db` in `auth.py` is a database concern and does not belong in `auth`. `GENERIC_ERROR` is vague, so `LOGIN_FAILED_MESSAGE` would be clearer.\n- **Divergent Change:** `auth.py` mixes DB connection handling, CSRF, session handling and the role guard. Moving `get_db` to `db.py` helps.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>53288</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>3</tool_uses><duration_ms>38951</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Standards review of uncommitted T01 work (read-only)**\n\n**Hard violations**\n1. **Secret key fallback.** `app/settings.py` falls back to `\"dev-only-not-for-production\"` when `CMS_SECRET_KEY` is unset. This line was not changed in the diff, but T01 is the first code to sign cookies with it. CLAUDE.md says to read secrets from the environment. With the fallback, anyone can forge a session cookie, including `user_id` and `csrf`, on a clone that has no `.env`. Fix: fail at startup if the variable is missing. Tests would set it in `conftest`.\n2. **Vocabulary.** CLAUDE.md says to use CONTEXT.md vocabulary and not to use two words for one thing. CONTEXT.md calls it **Sign-in** and **Sign-out**.\n   - The code uses both words: `NotSignedIn` and \"Sign in\" in the templates, but `/login`, `/logout`, `login.html`, `to_login`, `login_form`, `GENERIC_ERROR` and `test_t01_login.py`.\n   - Either rename the code to match the glossary or add \"login\" to the glossary.\n   - I'd rate this a soft violation, because the routes `/login` and `/logout` are probably fixed by the ticket.\n3. **Glossary filename conflict.** `docs/agents/domain.md` still says `GLOSSARY.md`, which contradicts the CLAUDE.md course rule. Not in the diff, but flag it.\n\n**Security checks (all pass unless noted)**\n- **CSRF:** `csrf_protect` is an app-wide dependency, so it covers every non-safe method, including the `/admin/{rest}` catch-all. It uses `compare_digest`. Both forms carry the token. Tests cover a missing token and a forged one.\n- **Session cookie:** HttpOnly is Starlette's default. `SameSite=lax` is set. `max_age=None` makes it a browser-session cookie. `https_only` is off, which is acceptable for a local-only console.\n- **Session fixation:** `request.session.clear()` runs at sign-in, so there is no fixation.\n- **Logout and replay:** the session is a client-side signed cookie. Logout only clears the cookie, so a replayed old cookie still works until it expires or the user is deactivated. This is a judgement call. The 2-hour idle limit and the per-request `active` check limit the exposure.\n- **Passwords:** argon2 hashes, a dummy hash on unknown emails, and one generic error message. Nothing logs passwords. `seed_demo` prints emails only.\n- **Dependencies:** `itsdangerous` and `argon2-cffi` are already in `pyproject.toml`, so nothing new was added.\n- **Relative paths:** `action=\"/login\"`, `action=\"/logout\"` and the redirects are absolute paths. They are in admin-only templates, which the hard constraint doesn't cover. Make sure `base.html` and these templates never get rendered into `site/`.\n\n**Smells (judgement calls)**\n- **Primitive Obsession and Shotgun Surgery:** the role strings `\"admin\"` and `\"editor\"` are repeated in the `db.py` CHECK, `User.role: str`, `require_role(\"admin\")`, `seed_users` and the conftest dict. A `Role` enum or constants would fix this.\n- **Duplicated Code:**\n  - `routes/auth.py` repeats `from app.main import templates` twice, inside the functions. This is a circular-import workaround, and the smell is the dependency from a route module back to `main`. Move `templates` into its own module such as `app/templating.py`.\n  - The `tests/conftest.py` `_csrf` helper duplicates `csrf_of` in `test_t01_login.py`.\n  - The `SELECT ... WHERE email` lookup in `users.py` is a minor repeat.\n- **Duplicated Code or Speculative Generality:** `Depends(auth.require_user)` is attached both on the `admin` router and on `admin_home`'s `user` parameter. The router-level one is redundant, though harmless, since FastAPI caches the dependency.\n- **Speculative Generality:** `require_role(*roles)` has no real caller; its only use is a probe in a test. It supports the later admin-only tickets, and the spec may require it. Check the spec. The `create_app(clock=...)` injection is justified by the idle-timeout tests.\n- **Mysterious Name:** `to_login` and `admin_unknown` are mild. `get_db` in `auth.py` is a database concern and does not belong in `auth`. `GENERIC_ERROR` is vague, so `LOGIN_FAILED_MESSAGE` would be clearer.\n- **Divergent Change:** `auth.py` mixes DB connection handling, CSRF, session handling and the role guard. Moving `get_db` to `db.py` helps.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>53288</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>3</tool_uses><duration_ms>38951</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>","reason":"absorbed_mid_turn","commandUuid":"ef74bf26-3151-4afd-ade2-632060c9887d","deliveryId":"f19b5933-4f3c-4860-b906-38047eae03e6"}

{"parentUuid":"9e4cf6be-9c75-481b-b824-6be2d76b9a7d","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg3HWm7daq8FwgZ1Z4qc8","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"T01 (ticket #2) is built and committed on `main` as `31bc8c4`, and the full suite passes (33 tests). The commit is local only; I haven't pushed it. Its message ends \"Closes #2\", so the issue won't close until it's pushed. I posted the `/code-review` findings on issue #2 before committing.\n\n**Checklist**\n- DONE: Users table with argon2 hashes and the Admin/Editor roles. `scripts/seed_demo.py` creates the President and Officer from the environment, and a second run changes nothing.\n- DONE: `/login` and `/logout`, signed-session cookies, and the generic \"Email or password is incorrect\" message.\n- DONE: a CSRF token check on every state-changing request. A POST without a valid token gets 403.\n- DONE: 2-hour idle sign-out, tested with an injected clock.\n- DONE: `require_user` and `require_role` guard in `app/auth.py`. Anonymous requests to any `/admin` path redirect to `/login`, including POSTs and unknown paths.\n- DONE: `client_as(\"admin\")` and `client_as(\"editor\")` work.\n- DONE: live check with uvicorn and curl: anonymous `/admin` redirects, and a signed-in user lands on `/admin`.\n- SKIPPED: ruff linting, because ruff isn't in the fixed dependency set.\n- SKIPPED: `PROJECT_STATE.md`, which doesn't exist in this repo.\n\n**Things you should know**\n- **T00 test changed:** I edited `test_admin_console_answers` to sign in as admin first. The ticket says anonymous `/admin` must redirect, and also that the T00 tests must still pass; those two can't both hold for that test. The assertions are unchanged, and the commit message and issue comment both say so.\n- **Open: secret key.** `CMS_SECRET_KEY` still falls back to a dev default, so session cookies are forgeable on a clone with no `.env`. Making the app fail at startup would break `cms serve` without a `.env`, so I left it for you to decide.\n- **Open: `GLOSSARY.md`.** `docs/agents/domain.md` and the stray `GLOSSARY.md` still use the wrong filename. That contradicts the CLAUDE.md rule, and I left it alone.\n- **Known limit:** a copied session cookie stays valid after logout until the idle timeout, because sessions are signed cookies rather than server-side records.\n- **`notes/usage-ledger.csv`:** it was already modified by the course hook, so it went into this commit.\n\nI also set `.claude/state/phase` to `T01` at the start of the session."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":764,"cache_read_input_tokens":90536,"output_tokens":881,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":764,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":881,"cache_read_input_tokens":90536,"cache_creation_input_tokens":764,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":764},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011Cg3HWkqkcYPJL1cRfLzYR","requestRef":"2b15061a-d122-45a0-88ca-7794deaa683d","requestedModel":"claude-sonnet-5-5","type":"assistant","uuid":"3da92405-e528-453e-8ed1-9952c8ac72a4","timestamp":"2026-10-15T03:07:43.203Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"4041ad69-0861-41ba-bd16-245831342e3a","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"4041ad69-0861-41ba-bd16-245831342e3a","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"acff3b3d-5cec-4aaf-81bf-8f787ed8774d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"23250ce4-a784-4c0e-b9b9-9beeffef65a8","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in the tracker doc.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nSearch the repo for every file that documents how code should be written. When `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` exists, it must be on the list.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\nIssue both sub-agent calls together, in the foreground, and aggregate the reports they return.\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"5fff5383-ca46-4aba-9770-5ff143a5ad61","timestamp":"2026-10-15T03:10:43.102Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"4041ad69-0861-41ba-bd16-245831342e3a","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}
