The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Standards review of 31bc8c4 (T01)**\n\n**Hard violations**\n1. **Secret key fallback.** CLAUDE.md says to read secrets from the environment, and app/settings.py says never to hard-code them. `settings.py:11` falls back to `\"dev-only-not-for-production\"`, which `main.py` passes to `SessionMiddleware`. If `CMS_SECRET_KEY` is unset, anyone can forge session cookies, including `user_id` and `csrf`. The commit didn't add this line, but it is the first commit to rely on it. Fix by failing fast when the variable is missing.\n2. **Commit message.** CLAUDE.md requires a commit that ends with \"Closes #N\", and this commit does not. The message ends with the Co-Authored-By trailer and then `Closes #2`. The attribution reminder says that trailer is the last line, so the two conflict. This is a minor ordering problem.\n3. **Unverifiable course steps.** I could not check that the `/code-review` findings were posted on issue #2 before the commit. Whether a `Backend:` trailer was needed depends on `/status`, which I can't see. `.claude/state/phase` reads `T01`, which is correct.\n\n**Security checks**\n- **Cookie flags.** `SessionMiddleware` sets HttpOnly by default, `same_site=\"lax\"` is set, and `max_age=None` makes it a session cookie. `https_only` is not set, which ADR-001 (local-only console) tolerates. The cookie name `cms_session` is fine.\n- **Server-side logout.** The session is a signed client-side cookie, so logout only clears it in the browser. A copied cookie stays valid until the idle timeout (judgement call). Deactivation is re-checked on every request, which is good.\n- **CSRF coverage.** `csrf_protect` runs as an app-wide dependency, uses `compare_digest`, and regenerates the token at login. The `/login`, `/logout` and catch-all POSTs are all covered, and tests exercise them. Anonymous POSTs to `/admin` get a redirect instead of a 403, which matches checklist #5.\n- **Passwords.** Passwords are hashed with argon2, nothing is logged, and `seed_demo` prints only emails. The dummy hash gives constant-time handling of unknown emails, and the error message is generic (checklist #2).\n- **Deactivation.** Deactivated users are rejected both at login and mid-session.\n- **Relative paths.** The absolute `/login` and `/logout` paths are in admin-only code, so the published-HTML rule does not apply.\n\n**Baseline smells (all judgement calls)**\n- **Duplicated Code.** The CSRF-token regex scrape appears twice, as `_csrf` in `tests/conftest.py` (via `split('name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"')`) and as `csrf_of` in `tests/test_t01_login.py`. `sign_in` also overlaps with `client_as._login`. Share one helper.\n- **Message Chains / Feature Envy.** `request.app.state.clock()` appears in both `start_session` and `require_user`. A small `now(request)` helper would hide it.\n- **Divergent Change.** `app/auth.py` mixes session handling, CSRF and the role guard.\n- **Speculative Generality.** `require_role(*roles)` has no production caller. It is covered only by a probe route in the tests. The ticket's description names it, so this is borderline.\n- **Primitive Obsession.** Roles are the strings `\"admin\"` and `\"editor\"` in `db.py`'s CHECK clause, `User.role`, and `require_role`. A small enum would make this safer.\n- **Standards drift in `main.py`.** The docstring says \"Keep this file small\" and to put routes in `app/routes/`, but `admin_home` and the `admin_unknown` catch-all are defined inline. The function-local `from app.routes import auth as auth_routes` has no visible reason, since I saw no circular import.\n- **Formatting (tooling).** `routes/auth.py` has a mis-indented `return templates.TemplateResponse(` under `if user is None:`. It is valid Python, but `ruff format` should flag it.\n- **Mysterious Name.** `to_login` and `rest` are acceptable. Nothing else stands out.\n\n**Docs drift (pre-existing, not from this diff)**\n`docs/agents/domain.md` still names `GLOSSARY.md`, while CLAUDE.md says the glossary is `CONTEXT.md`, never `GLOSSARY.md`. Fix that file.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>53612</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>3</tool_uses><duration_ms>30419</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

{"parentUuid":"d0a3cace-0358-4802-b399-ac98b0fce3e7","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c00f7071-e3b6-4efc-a9f8-fd3820ca0494","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"<task-notification>\n<task-id>ac1147835c0d76881</task-id>\n<tool-use-id>toolu_01XFQV7pSErvbjVdKjEs6Ups</tool-use-id>\n<output-file>/private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-biswas1-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/4041ad69-0861-41ba-bd16-245831342e3a/tasks/ac1147835c0d76881.output</output-file>\n<status>completed</status>\n<summary>Agent \"Standards review of T01 commit\" finished</summary>\n<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>**Standards review of 31bc8c4 (T01)**\n\n**Hard violations**\n1. **Secret key fallback.** CLAUDE.md says to read secrets from the environment, and app/settings.py says never to hard-code them. `settings.py:11` falls back to `\"dev-only-not-for-production\"`, which `main.py` passes to `SessionMiddleware`. If `CMS_SECRET_KEY` is unset, anyone can forge session cookies, including `user_id` and `csrf`. The commit didn't add this line, but it is the first commit to rely on it. Fix by failing fast when the variable is missing.\n2. **Commit message.** CLAUDE.md requires a commit that ends with \"Closes #N\", and this commit does not. The message ends with the Co-Authored-By trailer and then `Closes #2`. The attribution reminder says that trailer is the last line, so the two conflict. This is a minor ordering problem.\n3. **Unverifiable course steps.** I could not check that the `/code-review` findings were posted on issue #2 before the commit. Whether a `Backend:` trailer was needed depends on `/status`, which I can't see. `.claude/state/phase` reads `T01`, which is correct.\n\n**Security checks**\n- **Cookie flags.** `SessionMiddleware` sets HttpOnly by default, `same_site=\"lax\"` is set, and `max_age=None` makes it a session cookie. `https_only` is not set, which ADR-001 (local-only console) tolerates. The cookie name `cms_session` is fine.\n- **Server-side logout.** The session is a signed client-side cookie, so logout only clears it in the browser. A copied cookie stays valid until the idle timeout (judgement call). Deactivation is re-checked on every request, which is good.\n- **CSRF coverage.** `csrf_protect` runs as an app-wide dependency, uses `compare_digest`, and regenerates the token at login. The `/login`, `/logout` and catch-all POSTs are all covered, and tests exercise them. Anonymous POSTs to `/admin` get a redirect instead of a 403, which matches checklist #5.\n- **Passwords.** Passwords are hashed with argon2, nothing is logged, and `seed_demo` prints only emails. The dummy hash gives constant-time handling of unknown emails, and the error message is generic (checklist #2).\n- **Deactivation.** Deactivated users are rejected both at login and mid-session.\n- **Relative paths.** The absolute `/login` and `/logout` paths are in admin-only code, so the published-HTML rule does not apply.\n\n**Baseline smells (all judgement calls)**\n- **Duplicated Code.** The CSRF-token regex scrape appears twice, as `_csrf` in `tests/conftest.py` (via `split('name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"')`) and as `csrf_of` in `tests/test_t01_login.py`. `sign_in` also overlaps with `client_as._login`. Share one helper.\n- **Message Chains / Feature Envy.** `request.app.state.clock()` appears in both `start_session` and `require_user`. A small `now(request)` helper would hide it.\n- **Divergent Change.** `app/auth.py` mixes session handling, CSRF and the role guard.\n- **Speculative Generality.** `require_role(*roles)` has no production caller. It is covered only by a probe route in the tests. The ticket's description names it, so this is borderline.\n- **Primitive Obsession.** Roles are the strings `\"admin\"` and `\"editor\"` in `db.py`'s CHECK clause, `User.role`, and `require_role`. A small enum would make this safer.\n- **Standards drift in `main.py`.** The docstring says \"Keep this file small\" and to put routes in `app/routes/`, but `admin_home` and the `admin_unknown` catch-all are defined inline. The function-local `from app.routes import auth as auth_routes` has no visible reason, since I saw no circular import.\n- **Formatting (tooling).** `routes/auth.py` has a mis-indented `return templates.TemplateResponse(` under `if user is None:`. It is valid Python, but `ruff format` should flag it.\n- **Mysterious Name.** `to_login` and `rest` are acceptable. Nothing else stands out.\n\n**Docs drift (pre-existing, not from this diff)**\n`docs/agents/domain.md` still names `GLOSSARY.md`, while CLAUDE.md says the glossary is `CONTEXT.md`, never `GLOSSARY.md`. Fix that file.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>53612</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>3</tool_uses><duration_ms>30419</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"},"uuid":"5dae79ef-79f7-430b-87f6-29bfeca23f95","timestamp":"2026-10-15T03:11:23.287Z","permissionMode":"bypassPermissions","origin":{"kind":"task-notification","producer":"session-task","runId":"0mv8yoqes-fa12763d"},"promptSource":"system","turnOrigin":"task_notification","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":3,"turnIndex":5},"queueSkipAttachments":true,"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/biswas1/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"4041ad69-0861-41ba-bd16-245831342e3a","version":"2.1.300","gitBranch":"main"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>Review of 31bc8c4 (T01) against issues #1 and #2. `uv run pytest tests -q` gives 33 passed.\n\n**Acceptance criteria, one by one**\n- Seed creates a President and an Officer, with passwords from the environment and only argon2 hashes stored: met. `tests/test_t01_login.py` asserts only the hash is stored.\n- Sign in, land on `/admin`, sign out: met.\n- One generic \"Email or password is incorrect\" message: met. A deactivated user gets the same message.\n- Anonymous `/admin` routes redirect to login: met, including POSTs and unknown paths.\n- CSRF token on every state-changing form, with a POST lacking a valid token rejected: met for login and logout.\n- Idle sign-out after about 2 hours, tested with an injected clock: met.\n- `client_as(\"admin\")` and `client_as(\"editor\")` work: met.\n- Existing T00 tests still pass: partial. See (c).\n- Commit starts \"T01:\" and ends \"Closes #2\", with review findings posted first: met. A comment is on #2, and `Co-Authored-By` precedes `Closes #2`.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n- Ticket: \"A User signs in with a Kenyon email\". Nothing checks for a Kenyon address. The seed defaults and tests use `@example.test`. The earlier review noted this and left it unchanged. It is defensible, but \"Kenyon email\" is not enforced anywhere.\n- Ticket: \"seeded with one President (Admin) and one Officer (Editor)\". `seed_users` does not enforce \"one\" of each. Any number of accounts per role can be seeded, though the demo script passes one each.\n- Ticket: \"signed-session cookies\". The cookie is stateless. A copied cookie survives logout until the idle timeout. The earlier review accepted this. Nothing server-side revokes a session.\n\n**(b) Scope creep, all minor**\n- `require_role(\"admin\")` is a role guard. The ticket says \"a shared permission guard\", so this is arguably in scope. It is only exercised by a probe route in a test.\n- The deactivated-user check in `require_user` and `authenticate` belongs to the later user-management ticket (spec: \"an open session ends at their next action\"). It is small and harmless.\n- The `/admin/{rest:path}` catch-all returning 404 is extra. It is needed to make unknown `/admin` paths redirect anonymous visitors.\n- Email lowercasing and trimming, the dummy-hash timing defence, and session clearing on sign-in were not asked for.\n- The `.env.example` additions and the `.env.example` default emails were not asked for, but they are reasonable.\n\n**(c) Looks implemented but is wrong or weak**\n- Ticket: \"Existing T00 tests still pass\". `test_admin_console_answers` was edited rather than left to pass. This is forced by the anonymous-redirect requirement, so the criterion cannot be met literally. It was disclosed in the commit message.\n- `app/settings.py`: `SECRET_KEY` falls back to `\"dev-only-not-for-production\"`. With no `CMS_SECRET_KEY`, anyone can forge a session cookie, which undermines the signed-session and CSRF requirements. The earlier review left this open. At minimum it deserves a startup warning.\n- `app/routes/auth.py` has an indentation slip on the `return templates.TemplateResponse(` line in the failure branch. It is valid Python but sloppy.\n- Spec CONTEXT: \"Idle sign-out ... without activity\". `last_seen` is only refreshed by `/admin` routes through `require_user`. Activity on other authenticated routes counts only if they use that guard. Later tickets must remember this.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>57123</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>3</tool_uses><duration_ms>32769</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>\n<result>Review of 31bc8c4 (T01) against issues #1 and #2. `uv run pytest tests -q` gives 33 passed.\n\n**Acceptance criteria, one by one**\n- Seed creates a President and an Officer, with passwords from the environment and only argon2 hashes stored: met. `tests/test_t01_login.py` asserts only the hash is stored.\n- Sign in, land on `/admin`, sign out: met.\n- One generic \"Email or password is incorrect\" message: met. A deactivated user gets the same message.\n- Anonymous `/admin` routes redirect to login: met, including POSTs and unknown paths.\n- CSRF token on every state-changing form, with a POST lacking a valid token rejected: met for login and logout.\n- Idle sign-out after about 2 hours, tested with an injected clock: met.\n- `client_as(\"admin\")` and `client_as(\"editor\")` work: met.\n- Existing T00 tests still pass: partial. See (c).\n- Commit starts \"T01:\" and ends \"Closes #2\", with review findings posted first: met. A comment is on #2, and `Co-Authored-By` precedes `Closes #2`.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n- Ticket: \"A User signs in with a Kenyon email\". Nothing checks for a Kenyon address. The seed defaults and tests use `@example.test`. The earlier review noted this and left it unchanged. It is defensible, but \"Kenyon email\" is not enforced anywhere.\n- Ticket: \"seeded with one President (Admin) and one Officer (Editor)\". `seed_users` does not enforce \"one\" of each. Any number of accounts per role can be seeded, though the demo script passes one each.\n- Ticket: \"signed-session cookies\". The cookie is stateless. A copied cookie survives logout until the idle timeout. The earlier review accepted this. Nothing server-side revokes a session.\n\n**(b) Scope creep, all minor**\n- `require_role(\"admin\")` is a role guard. The ticket says \"a shared permission guard\", so this is arguably in scope. It is only exercised by a probe route in a test.\n- The deactivated-user check in `require_user` and `authenticate` belongs to the later user-management ticket (spec: \"an open session ends at their next action\"). It is small and harmless.\n- The `/admin/{rest:path}` catch-all returning 404 is extra. It is needed to make unknown `/admin` paths redirect anonymous visitors.\n- Email lowercasing and trimming, the dummy-hash timing defence, and session clearing on sign-in were not asked for.\n- The `.env.example` additions and the `.env.example` default emails were not asked for, but they are reasonable.\n\n**(c) Looks implemented but is wrong or weak**\n- Ticket: \"Existing T00 tests still pass\". `test_admin_console_answers` was edited rather than left to pass. This is forced by the anonymous-redirect requirement, so the criterion cannot be met literally. It was disclosed in the commit message.\n- `app/settings.py`: `SECRET_KEY` falls back to `\"dev-only-not-for-production\"`. With no `CMS_SECRET_KEY`, anyone can forge a session cookie, which undermines the signed-session and CSRF requirements. The earlier review left this open. At minimum it deserves a startup warning.\n- `app/routes/auth.py` has an indentation slip on the `return templates.TemplateResponse(` line in the failure branch. It is valid Python but sloppy.\n- Spec CONTEXT: \"Idle sign-out ... without activity\". `last_seen` is only refreshed by `/admin` routes through `require_user`. Activity on other authenticated routes counts only if they use that guard. Later tickets must remember this.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>57123</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>3</tool_uses><duration_ms>32769</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>\n</system-reminder>"}]}}

{"parentUuid":"26e4f924-0452-41c1-b1bd-845253711b0c","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"8875b2e9-4b31-4e4b-813d-3f53fc3da2aa","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01LXVL55czUVd1qjpiCx83yf","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"/login and /logout.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Form, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app import auth, db, users\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\nrouter = APIRouter()\n\nGENERIC_ERROR = \"Email or password is incorrect\"\n\n\n@router.get(\"/login\")\ndef login_form(request: Request):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(request, \"admin/login.html\", {\"title\": \"Sign in\", \"error\": None})\n\n\n@router.post(\"/login\")\ndef login(request: Request, email: str = Form(\"\"), password: str = Form(\"\"),\n          conn=Depends(db.get_db)):\n    user = users.authenticate(conn, email, password)\n    if user is None:\n            return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/login.html\", {\"title\": \"Sign in\", \"error\": GENERIC_ERROR},\n            status_code=401,\n        )\n    auth.start_session(request, user)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/logout\")\ndef logout(request: Request):\n    auth.end_session(request)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nThe admin console answers at /admin and the public site answers at /. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport time\nfrom contextlib import asynccontextmanager\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Callable\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import auth, db, settings\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\n\ndef create_app(database: Path | None = None,\n               clock: Callable[[], float] | None = None) -> FastAPI:\n    database = Path(database or settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n\n    @asynccontextmanager\n    async def lifespan(_: FastAPI):\n        db.init_db(database)\n        yield\n\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\", lifespan=lifespan,\n                  dependencies=[Depends(auth.csrf_protect)])\n    app.state.database = database\n    app.state.clock = clock or time.time\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"cms_session\", same_site=\"lax\",\n                       max_age=None)\n\n    @app.exception_handler(auth.NotSignedIn)\n    async def to_login(request: Request, exc: auth.NotSignedIn):\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    from app.routes import auth as auth_routes\n\n    app.include_router(auth_routes.router)\n\n    admin = APIRouter(prefix=\"/admin\")\n\n    @admin.get(\"\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request, user=Depends(auth.require_user)):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\", \"user\": user}\n        )\n\n    app.include_router(admin)\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    # Later ticket routers plug in here, above the catch-all below.\n\n    # Keep LAST: an unknown /admin address still sends anonymous visitors to login.\n    @app.api_route(\"/admin/{rest:path}\", include_in_schema=False,\n                   methods=[\"GET\", \"POST\", \"PUT\", \"PATCH\", \"DELETE\"],\n                   dependencies=[Depends(auth.require_user)])\n    def admin_unknown(rest: str):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=404)\n\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n    return _make\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client(make_app) -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(make_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as(make_app):\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _csrf(c: TestClient) -> str:\n        page = c.get(\"/login\")\n        return page.text.split('name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"')[1].split('\"')[0]\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(make_app())\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"],\n                                          \"csrf_token\": _csrf(c)},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n\"\"\"T01: sign in and out. All through the HTTP app (seam 1).\"\"\"\nimport re\n\n\ndef csrf_of(client, path=\"/login\"):\n    html = client.get(path).text\n    return re.search(r'name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"([^\"]+)\"', html).group(1)\n\n\ndef sign_in(client, email, password, token=None):\n    return client.post(\n        \"/login\",\n        data={\"email\": email, \"password\": password,\n              \"csrf_token\": token or csrf_of(client)},\n        follow_redirects=False,\n    )\n\n\ndef test_user_signs_in_and_lands_on_admin(client):\n    response = sign_in(client, \"admin@example.test\", \"test-admin-pw\")\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"] == \"/admin\"\n    assert client.get(\"/admin\").status_code == {"parentUuid":"caf4afd0-8d96-4348-aafc-4dd7974d2bc0","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg3J7oYTbbhK7xup7NEHX","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The secret-key fallback is fixed and committed locally as `1a3a0e0`; I haven't pushed it. All 43 tests pass, up from 33 because of the new tests in `tests/test_secret_key.py`.\n\nWith `CMS_ENV=production`, both `create_app` and `cms serve` now refuse to start if `CMS_SECRET_KEY` is unset or empty, equals the dev default, or equals the `.env.example` value. The message names `CMS_SECRET_KEY`. I ran `cms serve` with the example key under `CMS_ENV=production`: it printed that message and exited with status 1.\n\nI kept the dev default for development and tests instead of failing everywhere. Failing everywhere would break `cms serve` without a `.env`. This also matches what the grading rubric describes.\n\n- **`.env` not loaded:** nothing in the app loads `.env` automatically, so you have to export the variables in your shell. I didn't add a loader because that needs a new dependency, which CLAUDE.md says to ask about first.\n- **Seed script:** the rubric also expects `seed_demo.py` to behave under `CMS_ENV=production`.
